_comment: The Stones Are Dimming, Act I: Hearth and Stone (Ashford, age 8 to 12). Story v2: the warmth that makes the losses hurt (family supper, Thistle, Wren, Kindling Night). Seeds planted here pay off later: Idra's grey fingers (Act III twist), Bram's sums and his lantern 'for friends up north' (Act III betrayal, Act IV Hollin's Reach), the lantern for nobody (hidden ending). dialogue_runner.gd format; 'speaker' is a cast.json id.

lines.text: Stay in tonight, love. The Miller's Stone went out at supper.
Boots off, you're staying in. The Miller's Stone went out at supper.

choices.text: Went out? Stones don't go out.

lines.text: That's what I said. Warden Idra's up there now, glaring at it like it owes her money.
Nine guards. Forty-one stones. I count them at night, like sheep. Never once helped me sleep.
He's had five, sprout. Arithmetic's hungry work. Go on. Take a lantern.
From far away. Coat on. Back the moment she says so. And don't touch anything.
You're the child who keeps climbing my stones. Good. Come and hold the lantern.
The shrine child. You've the look. Good. Come and hold the lantern.
Nothing happened to it. That's the trouble. It simply stopped.
I can. My hands are slow tonight. Yours aren't.
Stone dust. Forty years of it. Don't stare, it's rude.
Palm flat on the cold side. Find the old cut with one finger. Down, across, up. Don't lift.
There. Hear that hum? That's the stone saying thank you. Rudely, but it counts.
Nobody carves the light, child. Old Hesk the miller rests in there. Forty years now.
When our people die, their ember can stay behind. In a stone, it keeps watch. That's the glow.
Some of him. The stubborn part. Stubborn lasts.
Ask me in daylight. Now run home. Something is pacing the ring edge, and it isn't a miller.
Feet! Plant your feet! ...Hm. Not bad. Not good. Not bad.
Maren Coldbrook. Old Mill Staff Yard. I teach children how not to die.
You swung with your eyes shut. Wolves notice things like that. Yard, at dawn.
Dawn. Bring water. Bring both arms, while you've still got them.
In the brambles, a stagborn fawn. Its antler-buds glow faint blue, like a stone at dusk. It's shaking.
A very small, very offended bleat. Then it follows you. It keeps following you.
It sits down in the road. It is home. You are home, apparently.
No. Absolutely not. It is NOT sleeping in the house.
It's sleeping in the house.
...Then it needs a name. Something prickly. Like its manners. And yours.
Staff up. You block with the wood, not your face.
Late. Wolves are never late. Staff up.
The Long Dark. Three stones failed on the Greenhollow road. I held one lit by hand till dawn.
Gave it what warmth I had. It took the arm as payment. Forty people slept that night. Fair trade.
Block when they commit. Roll when they're bigger than you. Everything is bigger than you.
So you're Aunt Maren's new stray. I'm Wren. I'm going to knock you over now.
She does. Twice. The second time, you take her down with you.
Everything's bigger than you, she says. Except me. I'm exactly your size. Friends?
Kindling Night. One lantern for each of ours who rests in a stone. This one's your grandfather.
Loud. Snored like a millstone. Held a wall the winter I was born. Hang it high, sprout.
Captain hangs his last. Same as every year. For friends up north.
Ones I couldn't count to in time. Here. Have a honey cake. It's a party.
Hm. Every stone with a family gets a lantern. The ones with nobody just get the dark.

choices.text: Then I'll hang one for nobody.

lines.text: ...Hm. Your mother raised you wrong. Good. Hang it by the Miller's Stone.
Thistle eats a lantern. Most of a lantern. The paper part, and a little of the candle.
Twelve. Tomorrow the ring asks what you are. Don't answer it. Let it answer you.
Then you'll be like me. The ring said nothing to me at twelve. I carve anyway.
Look at you. Twelve, and every stone in the ring lit up at once.
Your hair is still smoking. Was that you? That was you. Oh, love.
The rain stopped mid-fall. Right over you. I saw it. Everyone saw it.
Every banner in the square turned to face you. Every single one.
The ground hummed under my feet. Like the stones do. Like you do, now.
Nothing came, and you stood there anyway, chin up. I have never been prouder.
Saw it. Nearly dropped my spear. Don't tell the Captain.
Saw you stand there with nothing and not flinch. That's the harder trick, sprout.
Every stone in the Vale flared tonight. Not just ours. Every one.
It's a stone clearing its throat before bad news. Grow up quickly, apprentice. Not too quickly.
So. You glow now. Insufferable. I'm coming on every road you walk, to keep you humble.
Nothing came, and you stood there like a stone. Best thing I ever saw. I'm coming on every road.
